title: A 15-Pound Monkey Can Be Heard 3 Miles Away. It Pays a Price

scenes.text: A fifteen-pound monkey you can hear three miles away.
The howler monkey. Its roar carries up to five kilometers through dense rainforest. The secret is in its throat.
That's the hyoid, a hollow throat bone. Cambridge scientists scanned 250 of them. The biggest was ten times the size of the smallest.
Then they noticed the pattern. The species with the biggest, deepest roars had the smallest testes.
Evolution gave each one a budget. Spend it on a roar that scares rivals away, or on competing after the fight. Never both.
So one of the loudest animals on land is loud because it can't afford to fight. Three miles of sound, one trade.

description:
A howler monkey weighs about 15 pounds, yet its roar carries up to 5 kilometers, about 3 miles, through dense rainforest.
The sound comes from an enlarged hyoid bone in the throat. In 2015 Cambridge researchers scanned over 250 howler hyoids and found a ten-fold size range, and a strict trade-off: species with larger hyoids and deeper roars had smaller testes. Published in Current Biology.
Which animal would you have guessed was the loudest in the jungle?
subject: howler monkey
first_comment: Species that live in groups with one male roar the loudest. Species with many males per group roar less and compete another way. Which animal sound would you least like to wake up to?
